On the Motion of the Heart, etc.

Since these things are so, it is clear that another point will also be confirmed, which I previously stated: that blood passes continuously through the heart. For we see in the state of the body that blood flows from the arteries into the veins, not from the veins into the arteries. Furthermore, we see that almost the entire mass of blood can be drained from the arm itself, provided a proper ligature is applied and a single cutaneous vein is opened with a lancet. We also see that it is poured out so forcefully and abundantly that it is evident that not only is the blood which was contained in the arm below the ligature before the incision quickly and shortly evacuated, but the blood is drawn from the entire arm and the whole body, from the arteries as well as the veins.

Therefore, it is necessary to confess, firstly, that it is supplied with force and impetuosity, and is driven by force

<summary>Harvey argues that blood circulates from arteries into veins rather than the reverse, evidenced by the rapid drainage of the body's blood volume through a single opened vein under controlled ligature.</summary>
